content.text: The refusals come from two things in `room-3.mjs`. The hearth part already lays the range at x7..8 z29 (furnace, smoker, brick hob at y7), so the room's `F`/`S` cells sit one column off and collide with it. The second `layers()` call also passes origin y 6, so the "top" layer lands at y 6 instead of y 7. I'll fix both.

input.summary:
Wing kitchen and scullery (parts/room-3.mjs) now places 22 blocks with 0 refused and no off-palette blocks. The range (x7..8 z29) is left to the hearth part.
Cause: the room's furnace/smoker cells were one column off the hearth's range, and its second layers() call used origin y 6, so the table top landed at y 6.
make.sh completes and writes build.nbt.

waste.what: Found the y-offset bug by reading layers() source and tracing each layer's y by hand, after the refusal list only showed the symptom (7,6,29).
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls: read the module, read hearth.mjs, read layers() in the library.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`-style occupancy dump per room that prints each earlier part's blocks on the room's floor and layer rows (y6, y7) next to the room's own legend, so a collision and a wrong layer origin show up in one view.

waste.what: Mapped the legend characters to x,z by hand ("bFS..." at z29 puts F at x6 and S at x7) and compared against the hearth's coordinates.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate lookups by hand, one make.sh rerun to confirm.
waste.tool: A layers() dry-run mode that returns the cell list it would write (x,y,z,block) and checks each against the grid's current contents before writing, so the fix is visible without a full build.

waste.what: Computed the y offset of the second layer by reading layers()'s dy argument; the layer index is added to the origin's y, so the second call needed [x, y+1, z] with no way to tell from the output that y was wrong.
waste.tool: A layer helper taking an explicit y per layer (layerAt(y, rows, legend)), so the level is named at the call site instead of implied by an origin array.

companions.task: Confirm the wing range footprint (furnace and smoker at x7..8 z29, brick hob at y7) before the room's counters and pantry are laid, so the room's cells are set around it rather than over it.

left: Other parts still refuse writes into earlier parts (they are not mine to fix and I did not touch them): Chimneys, hearths and lights (7,26,30 and 8,26,30 brick_slab); Grounds and garden (20..21, 5, 13..14 gravel over bricks); room: Keeper's aisle (12,11,17 lantern and 12,12,17 iron_chain over iron_chain).

waste.tool: A layers() dry-run mode that returns the cell list it would write (x,y,z,block) and checks each against the grid's current contents before writing, so the fix is visible without a full build.

waste.what: Computed the y offset of the second layer by reading layers()'s dy argument; the layer index is added to the origin's y, so the second call needed [x, y+1, z] with no way to tell from the output that y was wrong.
waste.tool: A layer helper taking an explicit y per layer (layerAt(y, rows, legend)), so the level is named at the call site instead of implied by an origin array.

companions.task: Confirm the wing range footprint (furnace and smoker at x7..8 z29, brick hob at y7) before the room's counters and pantry are laid, so the room's cells are set around it rather than over it.
